title: Analytics query proxy with tenant scoping and per-route authorization
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Build a lightweight analytics query proxy that enforces tenant-scoped access controls and per-route authorization for all analytics and usage endpoints. This proxy will sit in front of existing analytics microservices (usage-aggregator, event-query, billing-views) and perform the following: 1) authenticate incoming requests (API token/service identity), 2) resolve tenant and role membership from entitlement services, 3) apply per-route and per-field access rules (masking/filtering where necessary), 4) inject tenant scoping filters into queries to prevent data leakage, and 5) emit audit events and metrics for access decisions. Goal: centralize enforcement to avoid repeated RBAC logic across multiple services while keeping request latency under 25ms median for cached checks and <75ms for first-time lookups.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy deployed behind console-api in staging and handling analytics routes
All analytics endpoints reject requests from identities without the appropriate tenant role
Query responses never return rows outside the authenticated tenant scope in randomized tests
End-to-end e2e tests cover per-field masking for PII (customer_email, user_ip) and pass in CI
Audit events (allow/deny) are emitted to the audit-log stream for every request
Latency SLOs: median auth latency <25ms (cold lookups <75ms) and <1% error rate under 95th percentile load
migration_plan: 1) Launch proxy in passive mode (log-only) for two weeks against staging traffic. 2) Run randomized replay tests that inject cross-tenant rows to validate filter injection. 3) Enable enforce mode with a small canary for 10% of requests. 4) Expand to 100% after 72h of stable metrics and sign-off from security and PM. 5) Deprecate in-service RBAC checks in dependent services once proxy is audited and rolling update completed.
rollout_plan: Gradual ramp to 100% over 48h with automated rollback on policy violations: 2026-02-26
Post-rollout 1 week review and cleanup of duplicated RBAC code: 2026-03-05
monitoring: Metric: audit-events.emitted counter broken down by decision (allow/deny)
Spot-check dashboard: cross-tenant-leak-detection which runs daily randomized queries
implementation_notes: Auth model: prefer service-to-service mTLS + short-lived service tokens for internal calls; API keys remain for external console clients
Entitlement lookup: use cached local copy of entitlement graph with background refresh; TTL 60s for active tenants, 15m for inactive
RBAC expression language: adopt CEL for per-route predicates to allow expressive rules without recompiling services
Query scoping: inject deterministic WHERE clauses at the proxy layer for SQL-based services; use structured filters for document stores
Caching trade-offs: aggressive caching reduces latency but risks stale permissions — chosen TTLs balance safety vs performance; critical changes (role revokes) trigger cache invalidation via pub/sub
Masking strategy: proxy will mask sensitive fields by default for roles without 'view_sensitive' permission; downstream services keep original data but never exposed over the analytics routes
Failure modes: on entitlement service unavailability proxy will (configurable) fallback to either careful allowlist mode (deny by default) or cached allow — default is deny to avoid data leakage
Performance: route-level hotpath optimized in Rust; bulk queries profiled separately to ensure batching is not impeded
